newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia PM says EU accord ratification by end May.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia PM says EU accord ratification by end May.

text.p: Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek said on Tuesday parliament would approve the association agreement with the European Union by the end of May.
"The association agreement has to be ratified no later than May this year," Drnovsek said at the annual meeting of Slovenian diplomats in Ljubljana.
The association agreement, which is a trade and cooperation pact that carries with it a promise of eventual EU membership, was signed in June 1996 but still has to be endorsed by most EU members.
"The coalition agreement with the People's Party guarantees that ratification will take place as soon as possible," Drnovsek said.
In February, Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats formed a coalition government with the conservative People's Party.
The People's Party was last year sceptical of the EU association accord, claiming Slovenia should first protect its national interests, especially agriculture, before joining the EU.

Slovenia is the first of the successor states of former Yugoslavia to have signed an EU association agreement, while nine other ex-communists states -- Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia, Romania and Bulgaria -- have already signed similar agreements.
Drnovsek reiterated Slovenia's other principal goal was membership of NATO.

"We will try to do everything to be in the first group of countries that will extend NATO....thereby strengthening the position of Slovenia in the world, reducing its political risks and so bringing about some economic advantages," Drnovsek said.
